property_summary: After any call to setOwner, the owner must remain unchanged if the caller is not the current owner; the buggy version allows a non-owner to change it.
After any call to setOwner, the previous owner must remain able to change the owner again; the buggy version allows the previous owner to be permanently locked out if a non-owner changes it.

After a successful call to setOwner by any sender, the new owner must equal the argument passed; the buggy version maintains this, but the reference version only allows the current owner to succeed and leaves owner unchanged otherwise.
After any call to setOwner by a non-owner, the owner state variable remains unchanged in the reference version, but the buggy version incorrectly sets the owner to msg.sender (the non-owner caller).
For any call to setOwner that does not revert, the return value must be true; the buggy version returns false for any such call, violating the rule.

After any call to setOwner, the owner must remain the original deployer, because the reference onlyOwner modifier requires the caller to be the current owner, which is never set to anything else; the buggy modifier allows anyone to call setOwner and change owner to the supplied address.
The reference contract ensures only the current owner can call setOwner (owner remains unchanged otherwise), while the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner to any address.
